definition: A semantic region is a deliberately coarse, mutually exclusive movement class shared by phases from different source motions. Rules are evaluated in order; the first match wins.
purpose: The source phase descriptions remain the detailed ground truth. These shared regions make cross-motion retrieval, held-out classification, and unsupervised-cluster agreement measurable without pretending that two differently worded descriptions are different classes.

regions.name: jumping
regions.description: Intentional jumps, whether traveling or in place.

regions.name: loaded_locomotion
regions.description: Locomotion while manipulating, holding, or supporting an object or environmental control.

regions.name: turning_locomotion
regions.description: Locomotion whose defining change is root heading or a curved path.

regions.name: backward_sideways_locomotion
regions.description: Locomotion primarily backward, diagonal, or sideways.

regions.name: forward_locomotion
regions.description: Remaining locomotion, predominantly forward or starting and stopping a forward gait.

regions.name: lowered_manipulation
regions.description: Object interaction while stooped, crouched, or substantially lowered.

regions.name: upright_manipulation
regions.description: Remaining object or environment interaction without purposeful root locomotion.

regions.name: gesture
regions.description: Expressive or bodily action without object or environment manipulation.

regions.name: transition
regions.description: A recovery, start, stop, or hand-lowering interval not captured by the movement-first rules above.
